messages.subject: Most appropriate cross type?
parts:
Hi Karl,

I am having trouble figuring out which, if any, cross type I should be using for my particular crossing design. 
The individuals that I have phenotype/genotype data for are the progeny of intercrossed individuals from distinct RIL populations. 
Starting from 4 inbred lines, I created three RIL populations. One inbred line (yellow in the attached image) was crossed to each of the three other inbred lines (shades of red in the attached image).  After these F1 lines were selfed to F6, individuals from different RIL populations were intercrossed. These F1s from crosses between RIL individuals is what I have genotyped/phenotyped.
So, there are four possible genotypes in an individual in each of these groups and 7 possible genotypes in the whole population.
Is there a cross type that would be compatible with this type of design?

Thank you!
Sam

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Most appropriate cross type?
parts:
We don't really have a cross type that fits. There's nothing in R/qtl2 for RIX populations.

I would use the genotype data on the group 1, 2, and 3 RILs to get genotype probabilities for the parents of the RIX.
You could then combine those probabilities to get probabilities for the RIX population, but R/qtl2 doesn't currently have any facilities to help.

karl
